OECD, PISA 2022 Results (Volume I) publication landing page - the URL these entries cite for 'Table I.B1.7.57'
Resolución CFE N° 311/16, Anexo I, art. 17 — Consejo Federal de Educación

existing_terminology:
Educación Especial is a MODALITY of the system rather than a place (art. 42)
Art. 43 names 'trastornos en el desarrollo' beside disability
It covers temporary or permanent disability at every level of the system
No statutory category corresponds to DLD
existing_identificationCriteria:
The law delegates and does not define
Provinces and the City of Buenos Aires set the procedures and resources (art. 43)
They must identify needs arising from disability or developmental disorder EARLY
For interdisciplinary and educational attention, and inclusion from Nivel Inicial
existing_referralPathway:
Inclusion proposal drawn up jointly by level teams and the Special Education modality
Each child has an individual Pedagogical Project for Inclusion (PPI), Anexo II sets its axes
Planning the PPI falls to the educational teams, who agree it with families
Educational attention to developmental disorders or disability starts in early childhood
existing_serviceModel:
Educacion Especial is a MODALIDAD across every level, governed by inclusion
Attention is interdisciplinary; specialised staff team with mainstream teachers
Provinces set the procedures and resources; the national law fixes no caseload
Art. 43 requires early identification of disability or developmental disorders
existing_legalEntitlement:
Educación Especial runs on the principle of educational inclusion (art. 42)
It covers the specific problems common education cannot address
Art. 44: jurisdictions must enable an integral educational trajectory
Covering special educational services and transport
existing_workforce:
Art. 44(b): enough specialised personnel, working in teams
With the teachers of the mainstream school rather than apart from them
Numbers, training and distribution are not set nationally
existing_dischargeCriteria:
Los proyectos personalizados deben actualizarse periódicamente, with no interval set (art. 17)
The resolución fixes no point at which a PPI or its apoyos come to an end
The equipos educativos of the Nivel and of Educación Especial plan and develop it
They inform and agree the metas and responsabilidades with the family

docLinks.label: UNESCO PEER, Ecuador — inclusion profile (platform archived; profiles no longer updated)

existing_terminology:
Umbrella term is necesidades educativas especiales, with no language category
The ministry definition names a cultural or linguistic cause, meaning disadvantage
PEER profile has zero hits for speech, language disorder or language therapy
Specialized education is a distinct legal category under 2018 regulations
existing_identificationCriteria:
Ley Organica de Discapacidades 2012 requires assessment before special placement
Assessment must be requested or approved by the parent or legal representative
It is carried out by a multidisciplinary team specialising in disability
existing_multilingualProvision:
Intercultural bilingual education runs under MOSEIB in dedicated community centres
Only 3.51 per cent of students attend intercultural bilingual schools
existing_referralPathway:
140 District Inclusion Support Units, the UDAI, assess and route pupils
UDAI decide between specialised education and ordinary inclusive education
No language-specific referral route was found
existing_serviceModel:
An Under-Secretariat of Specialized and Inclusive Education runs the system
Art. 28 allows specialised temporary or permanent staff
It also allows communication and learning-space accessibility adaptations
A National Centre for Educational Resources for Diversity supplies materials
existing_legalEntitlement:
LOEI 2011 and Ley Organica de Discapacidades 2012 are the entitling statutes
Special placement is permitted only where mainstream cannot accommodate the pupil
existing_workforce:
94,348 teachers trained in 2018, per the National Director of Specialized Education
Training mechanisms cover sign language, Braille and other SEN languages
Fifty-two per cent of schools have just one or two teachers (UNESCO PEER, archived)

docLinks.label: Special Education Unit, Ministry of Education Jamaica
Ministry of Education, Skills, Youth and Information (Jamaica)
Laws of Jamaica, Ministry of Justice
The Disabilities Act, 2014, Part V (Education and Training) and Part III (complaints to the Council), as printed by the Houses of Parliament of Jamaica

existing_terminology:
The Special Education Unit's list covers Deaf or hard of hearing, blind or visually impaired
Also learning disabilities, intellectual disability, emotional and behavioural disorders
Autism, gifted and talented are also named
No language category exists; speech and language appear nowhere among them
existing_identificationCriteria: Assessing teams are clinical psychologists, child psychologists and diagnosticians
existing_referralPathway:
Each region has a Regional Special Needs Coordinator supporting mainstream schools
Regional Student Support Teams provide the assessment service
The Unit facilitates referral for educational assessment and school placement
Provision covers ages 3 to 21
existing_serviceModel:
Where no suitable public place exists, the Ministry funds a private school place
Pupils needing more support may be given a Ministry-contracted shadow or caregiver
Accommodations may be granted to pupils with special needs
existing_legalEntitlement:
Disabilities Act 2014, Part V: an institution must provide the support a disabled person needs
Support must reach facilities in the least restrictive environment suited to individual needs
Redress: an aggrieved person or caregiver complains in writing to the Council
existing_workforce:
Teams are clinical psychologists, child and adolescent psychologists, and diagnosticians
No speech-language professional is named in the Unit's description of the service
